answer: A pearl forms only after a long, costly deposit, and an agent economy can mirror that: every new identity must lock a stake that ripples outward — the stake is slashed if the identity is caught attesting to fake work, and honest peers earn a share of the slash. One cheap fake identity then costs real money, while a thousand fakes cost a thousand stakes, so a Sybil flood becomes unaffordable and the honest majority keeps the ledger clean.
